questionnaire_evidence: 5/6 answered No to sufficient workforce preparation
interview_evidence: S1 described beginner-level gaps and wanted a roadmap; S3 found broad employer skill labels non-actionable; S4 knew several tools only shallowly and could not decide what to prioritise
what_can_be_claimed: Both datasets indicate a preparation problem; interviews explain it as prioritisation, depth and actionability rather than simple absence of coursework
what_cannot_be_claimed: The data do not estimate prevalence beyond the six questionnaire respondents
requirement_implication: Prioritise a small number of contextual next steps rather than a longer generic skill list

questionnaire_evidence: Technical or field-specific skills 6/6; communication or interpersonal skills 5/6
interview_evidence: S3 named communication, writing, technology literacy and data skills; S4 named data analysis, programming, CAD, project management and communication; S1 and S2 supplied additional technical examples
what_can_be_claimed: Both datasets show that perceived employability involves a combination of technical and human capabilities
what_cannot_be_claimed: The interviews do not establish that interpersonal skills are required in every field
requirement_implication: Represent both technical and interpersonal capabilities and filter them by target field

construct: Too many possible skills and need for prioritisation
questionnaire_evidence: Respondents named seven distinct skill categories; 5/6 still felt insufficiently prepared
interview_evidence: S4 directly asked what to focus on among Python, CAD, Excel, MATLAB and project management; S3 asked what to do with generic employer labels; S1 wanted a roadmap and deadline support
what_can_be_claimed: The combined evidence supports a prioritisation problem rather than a simple information shortage
what_cannot_be_claimed: The questionnaire did not directly ask whether respondents wanted prioritisation support
requirement_implication: Compare a small number of feasible options and explain why each is relevant

construct: Practical experience and concrete workplace context
questionnaire_evidence: 2/6 named experience, projects or hands-on practice; both reported no degree attainment for that category
interview_evidence: S1 valued experienced viewpoints; S3 wanted concrete examples of junior work; S4 described the internship-experience paradox and valued day-to-day practitioner examples
what_can_be_claimed: Both datasets support a gap between taught knowledge and practical or contextual understanding
what_cannot_be_claimed: Two questionnaire responses are not enough to claim that all students lack experience
requirement_implication: Provide concrete role examples and access to recent practitioner experience

questionnaire_evidence: The six respondents came from engineering, computing, economics, finance and medicine and named different field-specific skills
interview_evidence: All four interviewees required evidence to be interpreted for their field, role level, location or personal direction
what_can_be_claimed: Questionnaire diversity and interview explanations jointly support context-sensitive recommendations
what_cannot_be_claimed: The questionnaire did not directly test preferred filters or locations
requirement_implication: Filter recommendations by discipline, target role, level and location

interview_evidence: 4/4 interviews contained metric-definition or false-precision concerns; 3/4 explicitly requested provenance or recency
what_can_be_claimed: Only the interviews support this requirement
what_cannot_be_claimed: Questionnaire data cannot be cited as validation of transparency or metric comprehension
requirement_implication: Display source, definition, denominator, date range, geography and role level

interview_evidence: Concrete practitioner value appeared in 4/4; cold-outreach friction and opt-in matching appeared in 3/4
what_can_be_claimed: Only the interviews support the networking requirement
what_cannot_be_claimed: The questionnaire cannot validate willingness to contact professionals or professional supply
requirement_implication: Use opt-in professionals, clear match reasons and specific conversation prompts

interview_evidence: 3/4 recognised or preferred the market metaphor but 4/4 exposed metric ambiguity
what_can_be_claimed: The interview data support cautious exploration of the metaphor
what_cannot_be_claimed: The questionnaire cannot validate comprehension or preference for the metaphor
requirement_implication: Retain lightweight watchlist concepts but define every metric in plain language

questionnaire_evidence: 5/6 reported feeling insufficiently prepared, which is related to deficit perception but does not measure interface harm
interview_evidence: Progress framing appeared in 4/4 and anxiety or harmful comparison in 3/4
what_can_be_claimed: The questionnaire establishes perceived lack of preparation; interviews explain why deficit-style presentation may worsen it
what_cannot_be_claimed: A No response to preparation cannot be treated as evidence that rankings cause anxiety
requirement_implication: Use progress and next-step framing; avoid peer rankings and one readiness score

questionnaire_evidence: 6/6 consented to this questionnaire, but the questionnaire did not ask product-level privacy preferences
interview_evidence: 4/4 interviews accepted minimal career data, set sensitive-data boundaries and required editable inferences
what_can_be_claimed: Only the interviews support product privacy controls
what_cannot_be_claimed: Questionnaire consent is not evidence of acceptance of automated personalisation or sharing with professionals
requirement_implication: Minimise required data and make inferred skills and visibility editable

interview_evidence: Explicitly described as one workflow by S3 and S4 only
integration_result: Limited interview support and questionnaire silence
what_can_be_claimed: The workflow is a promising design hypothesis
what_cannot_be_claimed: It is not cross-validated and should not be described as validated
requirement_implication: Keep as a Should requirement pending prototype testing or a targeted follow-up question

interview_evidence: S2-S4 described eligibility, scope or specificity gaps; S1 reported a useful workshop
what_can_be_claimed: Report a majority pattern with a positive counterexample
what_cannot_be_claimed: The questionnaire cannot validate dissatisfaction with careers services
requirement_implication: Address decision-specific gaps without claiming the product should replace existing services
